page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: AlCl₃ exists as Al₂Cl₆
steps.mark_note: The dimer and the reason for it
lines: Aluminium in AlCl₃ has only six valence
electrons, so it is electron deficient.
Each molecule donates a chlorine lone
pair to the aluminium of the other, so
both aluminium atoms reach an octet.
steps.why: The dimer exists because a six-electron aluminium atom can accept a lone pair, so writing the electron count first makes the bridged drawing follow from a reason instead of from memory.
common_mistakes: Drawing two AlCl₃ molecules side by side without joining them. They are held together through two bridging chlorine atoms.
Saying aluminium already has an octet in AlCl₃. It has six electrons, which is why the dimer forms.
steps.memory_tip: Six electrons on aluminium, one lone pair from chlorine, octet complete.
steps.margin_note: Write the words electron deficient. They carry the reason for the dimer.

steps.label: The bridged structure
steps.mark_note: The bridged structure with bond lengths

lines.text: Al₂Cl₆ has two bridging chlorine atoms

lines: Draw the two aluminium atoms with two
chlorine atoms between them, forming a
Give each aluminium two more chlorine
atoms, one above and one below the ring.
Each aluminium is sp³ and tetrahedral.
steps.why: Each bridging chlorine atom is shared between the two aluminium atoms, so its bonds are longer and weaker than the four terminal bonds, and marking the two lengths is what shows the bridge is different.
common_mistakes: Drawing all six Al–Cl bonds the same length. The two bridge bonds are longer, about 221 pm against 206 pm.
Drawing only one bridging chlorine atom. Two chlorine atoms bridge the two aluminium atoms.
Drawing the aluminium atoms flat. Each is sp³ and tetrahedral in the dimer.
steps.memory_tip: Four terminal chlorines outside and two bridging chlorines in the middle make six.
steps.margin_note: Mark both bond lengths on the sketch, 206 pm and 221 pm. Each bridging chlorine makes one ordinary bond and one coordinate bond, so draw one arrow from each.

insider_note: The two bridging chlorine atoms are the point of this drawing; a sketch with six equal Al–Cl bonds and no bridge shows a different molecule.
